'''Julian Thomas Peterson''' (born July 28, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for eleven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. Peterson was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the first round of the [[2000 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] and [[Detroit Lions]].

'''Quintorris Lopez''' "'''Julio'''" '''Jones Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|h|uː|l|i|oʊ}} {{respell|HOO|lee|oh}}; born February 8, 1989)<ref name=":0" /> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] who played in the  [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 13 seasons, primarily with the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]] where he won a national championship in [[2010 BCS National Championship Game|2009]], and was selected by the Falcons in the first round (sixth overall) of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. He is regarded as one of the greatest receivers of the <!-- DO NOT ADD "ONE OF THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME" THAT IS NOT TRUE. -->2<!-- DO NOT ADD "ONE OF THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME" THAT IS NOT TRUE. -->0<!-- DO NOT ADD "ONE OF THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME" THAT IS NOT TRUE. -->1<!-- DO NOT ADD "ONE OF THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME" THAT IS NOT TRUE. -->0s<!-- DO NOT ADD "ONE OF THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME" THAT IS NOT TRUE. -->.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=2019-12-26 |title=Top 10 receivers of the decade |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/top-10-receivers-of-the-decade |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030033550/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/12/26/top-10-receivers-of-the-decade/ |archive-date=October 30, 2020 |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

After a productive rookie season, Jones recorded 1,198 receiving yards and ten [[touchdowns]] in [[2012 Atlanta Falcons season|2012]] and was named to his first [[Pro Bowl]]. After an injury-plagued 2013 season where he only played five games, Jones led the Falcons in receiving yards in 2014, and made his second Pro Bowl, beginning to develop a deep chemistry with team [[quarterback]] [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moton |first=Maurice |date=June 4, 2019 |title=Ranking the NFL's Top 10 QB-WR Duos |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2838919-ranking-the-nfls-top-10-qb-wr-duos |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120033218/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2838919-ranking-the-nfls-top-10-qb-wr-duos |archive-date=January 20, 2022 |access-date=January 20, 2022 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mays |first=Robert |date=January 24, 2020 |title=The Top 10 NFL Quarterback–Pass Catching Duos of the 21st Century |url=https://www.theringer.com/nfl/2020/1/24/21079570/top-10-qb-receiver-tight-end-duos-peyton-manning-randy-moss-tom-brady-gronk |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704144255/https://www.theringer.com/nfl/2020/1/24/21079570/top-10-qb-receiver-tight-end-duos-peyton-manning-randy-moss-tom-brady-gronk |archive-date=July 4, 2022 |access-date=January 20, 2022 |website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]}}</ref> Jones broke out the next season, leading the league in receiving yards and co-leading in [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]], both of his statistics ranking top five all-time in a season. After this season, he was named to his first [[All-Pro]] selection. In [[2016 Atlanta Falcons season|2016]], Jones again had a productive year, garnering another All-Pro selection, and helped to lead the Falcons to [[Super Bowl LI]]. Over the next three seasons, Jones amassed 4,515 yards, the most by any player during that span, including leading the league again in yards in [[2018 NFL season|2018]].

Jones has amassed the most receiving yards by any player since entering the league,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most receiving yards since the 2011 NFL season |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/who-has-the-most-receiving-yards-since-2011-season |access-date=January 21, 2023 |website=[[StatMuse]] |language=en}}</ref> and more than any receiver in the 2010s, with 12,125 yards during that span.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most receiving yards by a player from 2010–2019 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/who-has-the-most-receiving-yards-in-the-2010s |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120033217/https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/most-receptions-yards-in-2010s |archive-date=January 20, 2022 |access-date=January 20, 2022 |website=[[StatMuse]]}}</ref> In doing so, Jones was invited to seven Pro Bowls, including six consecutive from 2014 to 2019, was a first-team All-Pro selection twice and was named second-team All-Pro three times.

Jones has been noted for having a rare combination of size (6 ft 3 in and 220 lbs), speed ([[40-yard dash]] in 4.39 seconds), catching ability, strength, leaping ability, and body control, which has drawn frequent comparisons to [[Calvin Johnson]].<ref name="Combine">{{Cite web |title=NFL Events: Combine Player Profiles – Julio Jones |url=http://www.nfl.com/combine/profiles/julio-jones?id=2495454 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108051641/http://www.nfl.com/combine/profiles/julio-jones?id=2495454 |archive-date=January 8, 2019 |access-date=January 7, 2019 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bardeen |first=Knox |date=February 1, 2013 |title=Why Julio Jones Is Better Than Calvin Johnson |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1511145-why-julio-jones-is-better-than-calvin-johnson |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814144159/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1511145-why-julio-jones-is-better-than-calvin-johnson |archive-date=August 14, 2021 |access-date=August 14, 2021 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> On November 11, 2018, Jones became the fastest player in NFL history to reach 10,000 career receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McClure |first=Vaughn |date=November 11, 2018 |title=Julio Jones becomes fastest receiver to 10,000 yards |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/atlanta-falcons/post/_/id/33343 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108045926/http://www.espn.com/blog/atlanta-falcons/post/_/id/33343 |archive-date=January 8, 2019 |access-date=January 7, 2019 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> On September 15, 2019, Jones became the all-time career receiving yards leader for the Falcons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Will |date=2019-09-16 |title=WATCH: Julio Jones scores 54-yard touchdown, surpasses Roddy White as Falcons' all-time leading receiver |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/watch-julio-jones-scores-54-yard-touchdown-surpasses-roddy-white-as-falcons-all- |access-date=2024-05-30 |website=[[Atlanta Falcons]] |language=en-US}}</ref> On October 5, 2020, Jones became the all-time career receptions leader for the Falcons. His career average of 87.9 receiving yards per game is the sixth-highest in NFL history, and as of 2025, he is tied for third all time in career games with 100-yards receiving with 59 career games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Receiving Yards per Game Career Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/rec_yds_per_g_career.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217215239/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/rec_yds_per_g_career.htm |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |access-date=September 14, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |publisher=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Most Career 100 Yard Receiving Games |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/most-career-100-yard-receiving-games |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220130181753/https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/most-career-100-yard-receiving-games |archive-date=January 30, 2022 |access-date=January 30, 2022 |website=[[StatMuse]]}}</ref> After another injury-plagued [[2020 Atlanta Falcons season|2020 season]], Jones was traded to the [[Tennessee Titans]] in 2021 after reported disgruntlement with Atlanta's new front office.<ref name="Titans trade">{{Cite web |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=June 6, 2021 |title=Falcons trade WR Julio Jones, future sixth-rounder to Titans for second- and fourth-round picks |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/falcons-trading-wr-julio-jones-to-titans |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806182630/https://www.nfl.com/news/falcons-trading-wr-julio-jones-to-titans |archive-date=August 6, 2022 |access-date=June 6, 2021 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref> After being released by the Titans in 2022, Jones signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] before being released at the conclusion of the 2023 season.
